# MyGirivalam.in

> MyGirivalam.in is a free digital companion for Girivalam — the sacred 14 km
> barefoot circumambulation (pradakshina) of Arunachala Hill in Tiruvannamalai,
> Tamil Nadu, India. It offers live GPS navigation of the Girivalam path, the
> locations and timings of the eight Ashta Lingam temples, Pournami (full moon)
> dates, Arunachaleswarar (Annamalaiyar) temple information, mantras, and
> practical pilgrim resources (water, food/annadhanam, rest, medical, parking).

## Key facts
- Girivalam is walked clockwise around Arunachala Hill, starting and ending near the Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai.
- The full path is approximately 14 km and passes eight Ashta Lingam shrines (Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirudhi, Varuna, Vayu, Kubera, Esanya Lingam), each aligned to a compass direction.
- Girivalam is traditionally performed on Pournami (full moon) nights, when hundreds of thousands of devotees walk the path.
- The site is a guide/utility, not an official temple authority; timings can change on festival days.

## Core pages
- [Home](https://mygirivalam.in/): Overview of Girivalam tools and resources.
- [Girivalam Live GPS Map](https://mygirivalam.in/girivalam-map): Real-time navigation of the 14 km path and all Ashta Lingam temples.
- [Spiritual Guide](https://mygirivalam.in/girivalam-guide): Stories, mantras, and the meaning of Arunachala and Girivalam.
- [Girivalam Services](https://mygirivalam.in/girivalam-services): Practical services and help for planning a visit.
- [Pournami Dates](https://mygirivalam.in/pournami-dates): Full moon (Pournami) Girivalam dates for 2025–2026.
- [Next Pournami](https://mygirivalam.in/next-pournami): The next upcoming full moon Girivalam date.
- [Spiritual Resources](https://mygirivalam.in/spiritual-resources): Mantras, audio, and devotional material.
- [Emergency Contacts](https://mygirivalam.in/emergency-contacts): Safety and emergency information for pilgrims.

## Location
- Place: Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu, India
- Arunachaleswarar (Annamalaiyar) Temple coordinates: 12.2307, 79.0628
- The temple is one of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams, representing the fire (Agni) element.
